findings.title: Missing, unreadable or empty data for an area is reported as 'nothing needs attention' in that area
findings.location: app.js:221 (fetch has no res.ok check; any body goes to parseCSV); exceptions.js:22-33 (parseCSV accepts any text, no header or row validation); exceptions.js:141 (rows without status='open' are skipped silently); exceptions.js:82-89 + app.js:57 (budget NaN)
findings.repro: python3 -m http.server 8801 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory /home/claude/ranch-ops-dashboard & node docs/audit/diagnostics/states-check.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8801/ /tmp/out. Minimal case: page.route('**/data/health.csv', r => r.continue({ url: base + 'data/__missing_health.csv' })) returns the server's real 404 HTML. Same result with a 200 garbage body, or a 200 header-only body for health, budget, water or moves.
findings.expected: The page says that health.csv (or whichever file) could not be loaded or is empty. That area is not shown as clear, e.g. the chip reads 'Health (no data)' and there is no 'Nothing in health needs attention.'
findings.actual: "[health:404] ready=true pageErrors=0 rows=8 warnsUser=false ... chips: All (8), Water (3), Grazing (1), Gain (2), Health (0), Budget (2)" and "Needs attention: 8 (2 critical, 5 serious, 1 warning)". The only trace is a console message: "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found)". budget:404 gives "Budget (0)" and "Spend vs budget: −NaN% ($NaN of $NaN, season to date)". water:header-only gives "Water (0)" and "Water tanks OK: 0 of 0 (0 need a look)", with "0 critical". moves:header-only gives "Grazing (0)". health:garbage and health:header-only behave the same as health:404.
findings.consequence: The overdue yearling booster and the pinkeye check disappear from the morning list while the page looks normal and the as-of line is intact, so a manager who trusts the page skips a vet task. An empty water export hides a leaking tank and a tank at 11.8%. That is the opposite of what an exception report is for, and an interviewer testing failure modes would find it in one try.
findings.regression_test: Playwright with page.route on the real data, values checked against the CSVs. (1) health.csv to 404: expect visible text matching /health/i and /could not load|missing|unavailable/i, and expect the Health chip not to equal 'Health (0)'. With full data the Health chip is 'Health (2)': the booster is due 2026-09-15, 15 days overdue at 2026-09-30; pinkeye is due 2026-10-03, 3 days away. (2) water.csv body 'tank_id,pasture_id,time,level_pct\n': expect an error naming water.csv instead of 'Water tanks OK 0 of 0'. (3) Unit test: validateTable(parseCSV('<!DOCTYPE HTML>\n<html>'), ['group','task','last_done','next_due','status'], {minRows:1}) throws, and so does the header-only health text.
findings.proposed_fix: Load each file through a helper that throws on !res.ok, checks the required columns for that file, and requires at least 1 row (meta must have as_of). On failure, show a visible error card naming the file(s). Mark the affected areas' chips and tiles as 'no data' instead of computing exceptions from an empty table.

findings.title: Any other load failure leaves a blank skeleton forever, with no loading or error message
findings.location: app.js:221-225 (top-level await with no try/catch); index.html:72-112 (empty containers, no placeholder or loading text)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/states-check.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8801/ /tmp/out. Scenario 'loading': page.route('**/data/*.csv', async r => { await sleep(3000); r.continue(); }), snapshot at 1 s. Scenario 'water:abort': route.abort('failed') for water.csv. Scenario 'meta:404'.
findings.expected: While data loads, a visible loading message. If a file fails, a visible error naming the file. No uncaught exception.
findings.actual: loading: "ready=false pageErrors=0 rows=0 warnsUser=false loadingText=false"; only headings and notes are visible (state-loading.png). 24 of the 32 per-file failure scenarios end with "ready=false pageErrors=1", e.g. "[water:404] ... (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'localeCompare'))", "[health:abort] ... (Failed to fetch)", "[meta:header-only] ... (Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'as_of'))". The screen matches the loading state, and the as-of line is empty.
findings.consequence: On a weak connection, or if a file fails to deploy, the manager sees empty cards and can't tell 'still loading' from 'broken'. In a portfolio demo the page simply looks broken.
findings.regression_test: (1) Delay all CSVs 3 s: at 1 s expect text matching /loading/i inside #tiles or the Needs attention card. (2) water.csv aborted: within 2 s expect visible text matching /water\.csv/ and /could not load/i, and zero pageerror events. (3) meta.csv header-only: expect an error mentioning the as-of date instead of a blank page.
findings.proposed_fix: Put a 'Loading example data...' placeholder in the static HTML. Wrap the load-and-render block in try/catch and replace the placeholder with an error card listing the failed files and the error message. Reuse the per-file validation from the previous finding.

findings.title: Chart details cannot be reached by keyboard or screen reader
findings.location: app.js:83, 119, 155, 183 (svg role=img with a generic aria-label; no focusable marks; no focus handlers); app.js:26-32
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/browser-check.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8801/ /tmp/out. keyboardWalk presses Tab from the top and records activeElement and #tip each step. The inventory counts descendants of svg.chart with tabIndex >= 0.
findings.expected: Keyboard users can reach per-mark details or an equivalent data table for each chart.
findings.actual: "keyboard tooltips: {\"tabStopsInsideCharts\":0,\"tooltipShownOnAnyFocus\":false}". Desktop tab stops are steps 1-6 (the chips), then "7:body (focus left the page content)". focusableDescendants = 0 for all 11 charts. Only the budget chart has a data table.
findings.consequence: Water history, grazing dates and per-animal gain exist only in hover tooltips. A keyboard or screen-reader user gets 'Average daily gain per animal by group' and nothing more. This undercuts the README's accessibility positioning ('Severity is never color alone').
findings.regression_test: Tab past the last chip: focus reaches a control or mark in the gain chart. Focusing the H026 mark (or its table row) exposes 'H026 (Heifers) 0.11 lbs/day, Jul 20 to Sep 15'. Alternatively, each of the water, grazing and gain charts has an associated table in which T4 reads 'Sep 30, 6 PM: 10%' and Yearlings reads 'Sand Hills, Sep 6, 24 days of 21'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a 'Show data' toggle or a visually hidden table for each chart (water: latest level and 24 h drop; grazing: current stay vs plan; gain: group average plus slow tags). Optionally make key marks focusable (tabindex=0) with focus/blur handlers that place the tooltip at the mark.

findings.title: On a phone the 'Problem' and 'First step' columns are off-screen and budget differences are cut mid-number
findings.location: index.html:45 (.scroll { overflow-x: auto }); app.js:66-69 (5-column exceptions table); app.js:203-205 (budget table)
findings.repro: browser-check.mjs phone viewport, overflow(). The screenshots <scratch>/audit/baseline/extra/phone-card-exceptions.png and phone-card-budget.png (from extra/sections.mjs) show it.
findings.expected: At 390 px every exception row shows what is wrong and the first step without sideways scrolling, and dollar values are fully visible.
findings.actual: "exceptions: scrolls=true cut=[Problem,First step]" (clientWidth 316, scrollWidth 413). "budgetTable: scrolls=true cut=[Difference]" (316 vs 330). The screenshots show 'DIFFERENC' and '+$1,80'. There is no visible cue that the table scrolls.
findings.consequence: The README's main design point is that every row says what to do so it can go to a crew lead. On a phone, the 'what to do' column is hidden and over-budget amounts are truncated.
findings.regression_test: At 390x844, for every th in #exceptions and #budgetTable, th.getBoundingClientRect().right <= its .scroll container's right + 1, or with a stacked layout each row's First step text is inside the viewport. The Repairs Difference cell '+$1,800' (9,000 - 7,200) is fully inside its container.
findings.proposed_fix: Below ~600 px, render each exception as a stacked row: severity + subject, then the problem, then the first step. Drop the Area column there, since the chips already show area. Tighten the budget table, e.g. drop the Budget column on narrow screens or shrink the font and padding.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is lost after activating a filter chip
findings.location: app.js:62-65 (chips rebuilt via innerHTML on every click); app.js:224
findings.repro: browser-check.mjs chipKeyboardActivation: blur, Tab until data-a=Water, press Enter, read activeElement, press Tab.
findings.expected: After Enter, focus stays on the Water chip (aria-pressed=true), and the next Tab goes to Grazing.
findings.actual: Both viewports: "{\"focusedBeforeEnter\":\"button.chip[data-a=Water] \\\"Water (3)\\\"\",\"afterEnter\":{\"active\":\"body\",\"pressed\":[\"Water (3)\"]},\"afterNextTab\":\"button.chip[data-a=All] \\\"All (10)\\\"\"}". After a mouse click, activeElement is also 'body'.
findings.consequence: Keyboard users lose their place after each filter and must tab from the start. Screen-reader focus jumps to the document body.
findings.regression_test: Tab, Tab, Enter: expect document.activeElement.dataset.a === 'Water' and aria-pressed 'true'. Press Tab: expect data-a 'Grazing'.
findings.proposed_fix: Render the chips once and update only aria-pressed and the counts. Or, after re-rendering, focus the button whose data-a equals the selected area.

findings.actual: Desktop: "\"3.0\" x \"lbs per day\" (20 px2)". Phone: the same, at 12 px2. At phone width "T6 Cedar Draw no signal" is 40.3 px tall and every other header is 20.1, so the T6 chart starts lower than T5's (visible in phone-card-water.png).
findings.consequence: Small polish issues that a reviewer notices on the first scroll.
findings.regression_test: In #gain svg, no two text bounding boxes intersect (today there is 1 pair). At 390 px, all 8 .mini h4 heights are equal (20.1 px).
findings.proposed_fix: Move 'lbs per day' below the tick row (raise m.b) or anchor it at the left. Give the h4 name span white-space:nowrap with text-overflow:ellipsis, or use a shorter 'silent' label.

findings.title: Exception text shows raw ISO dates while the rest of the page uses 'Jul 20'
findings.repro: Load the page (any viewport) and read the exceptions table. browser-check.mjs reports it in inventory.exceptionTable.
findings.expected: The same date format as the tiles and tooltips, e.g. 'since Jul 20' and 'due Sep 15'.
findings.actual: "0.44 lbs/day since 2026-07-20 vs 1.0 target", "Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15)", "Due in 3 days (2026-10-03)". The tile says "since Jul 20". On a phone the dates wrap as "2026-" / "07-20" (phone-card-exceptions.png).
findings.consequence: Minor inconsistency in the table meant to be handed to a crew lead.
findings.regression_test: The Heifers row's problem text contains 'since Jul 20' (the second-to-last weigh-in in weights.csv is 2026-07-20). The health rows contain 'Sep 15' and 'Oct 3'. The existing tests match on subject, so they still pass.
findings.proposed_fix: Format these dates with a shared short-date helper (en-US month and day) in exceptions.js.

findings.title: All-clear copy reads 'Nothing in all needs attention.' and the budget tile shows '−0.0%'
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/states-check.mjs ... scenario 'all-clear' (the data edited in flight so no rule fires)
findings.expected: 'Nothing needs attention.' for All, and '0.0%' when spend equals budget.
findings.actual: "empty message: \"Nothing in all needs attention.\"" and "Spend vs budget: −0.0% ($88,400 of $88,400, season to date)".
findings.consequence: The 'good day' state, which a demo viewer might see if thresholds are tuned, reads awkwardly.
findings.regression_test: With the all-clear data: the table message equals 'Nothing needs attention.', and the tile value equals '0.0%' (88,400 - 88,400 = 0). Clicking Water still shows 'Nothing in water needs attention.'
findings.proposed_fix: Special-case area === 'All'. Choose the sign as ta > tb ? '+' : ta < tb ? '−' : ''.

findings.title: 'Head on grass 375' counts 180 cow-calf pairs as 180 head
findings.location: app.js:53-55 (head = sum of groups.head); data/groups.csv ('Cows,cow-calf pairs,180')
findings.repro: Load the page and read the second tile
findings.expected: Either '180 pairs' with calves counted, or a label that does not imply a total head count.
findings.consequence: A ranch reviewer may read 375 as leaving out the roughly 180 calves on the place. This is a domain judgement, not a code error.
findings.regression_test: The tile detail reads '180 pairs' (groups.csv class 'cow-calf pairs', head 180). Or, if calves are counted, the total is 180 x 2 + 45 + 150 = 555 under a one-calf-per-pair assumption stated in the README.
findings.proposed_fix: Change the wording to '180 pairs, 45 heifers, 150 yearlings', and either rename the tile (e.g. 'Cattle on grass') or count calves and say so.
